predecessors.name: Yuan dynasty
predecessors.text: the Mongolian core of the Yuan (Shangdu, Yingchang, Karakorum), retained when the court left Dadu in September 1368

successors.name: Four Oirats
successors.text: the Mongolian steppe under Esen's Oirats, 9,639 of the Northern Yuan's last 9,642 cells

ledger.x: September 1368: Toghon Temur flees Dadu for Shangdu as Ming forces approached, and the Yuan court continues on the steppe.
1369: the court moves from Shangdu to Yingchang.
1370: the Ming take the Inner Mongolian capitals.
18 May 1388: the Ming win at Buir Lake.
1402: the western steppe passes to the Oirats on Cliopatria's map (4,302 cells fewer; 3,352 inside the Four Oirats' first shape).
1415: 397 cells of the south-west edge pass to the Ming on Cliopatria's map.
1439: Esen's Oirats take the khanate's lands.

wars.name: Ming-Northern Yuan wars of the Hongwu reign
wars.outcome: The Ming take Shangdu and Yingchang (1369-1370), Toghon Temur dies at Yingchang in 1370, Biligtu's general Koke Temur defeats a Ming pursuit in 1372, the Ming sack Karakorum in 1380 and withdraw, Naghachu surrenders in 1387 and the Ming win decisively at Buir…

wars.name: Ming conquest of Yunnan
wars.outcome: Yuan loyalists under Basalawarmi in Yunnan and Guizhou are defeated and killed.

wars.name: Battle of Buir Lake
wars.outcome: 18 May 1388: Ming victory; about 80,000 Mongols captured, Togus Temur murdered by Yesuder on the Tula river.

wars.name: Oirat ascendancy over the Mongol khanate
wars.outcome: After 1388 the Oirats become kingmakers, take the Altai and western Mongolia (Cliopatria 1402), install and depose Borjigin khans (Mahmud's puppet at Karakorum in 1412; Delbeg enthroned by Bahamu's Oirats in 1412) and under Esen (taishi from 1438) rule the…

wars.name: Ming expeditions of the Yongle Emperor into Mongolia
wars.outcome: A Ming army is defeated in September 1409 (its commander Qiu Fu dies; 'Battle of Kherlen in 1409' on the Northern Yuan page); the emperor defeats Oljei Temur and Arughtai in March 1410, campaigns again in 1414, 1422, 1423 and 1424 (dying on 12 August 1424 at…

certainty.note: Steppe, Gobi and forest frontiers throughout, drawn approximate; the Ming wall frontier south of Shangdu is the firmest edge but no page gives a line.
